 SSC releases Aadhaar-based biometric authentication guidelines for CGL, CHSL, MTS and other exams; details here
 SSC has asked candidates to keep their Aadhaar biometrics permanently unlocked during recruitment exams to avoid identity verification problems at exam centres. Temporary unlocking may not be enough.
 Curated by Yash Wardhan Singh 
 Image: iStock 
 Nov 18, 2026
 Share
 The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has released new rules for Aadhaar biometric verification for candidates appearing in its recruitment exams. These include the Combined Graduate Level (CGL), Combined Higher Secondary Level (CHSL), Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), GD Constable, Central Police Organisation (CPO) and Junior Engineer (JE) examinations. 
 In a notice issued on November 17, the commission has asked candidates to keep their Aadhaar biometrics permanently unlocked during the entire examination process. It has warned that the temporary unlocking option, which remains active for only 10 minutes, may not be enough to complete all identity checks at exam centres. 
 As per the SSC notice, candidates must make sure that their Aadhaar details are correct and updated. This includes personal information such as name, date of birth and address. They must also update their biometric details, including fingerprints, iris scans and facial information. 
 The commission explained that the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) offers two options to unlock Aadhaar biometrics: temporary and permanent. However, the temporary option is valid for just 10 minutes. This period may not be enough for the different identity verification steps at examination centres. 
 SSC Aadhaar biometric verification: Important instructions for candidates 
 SSC has advised candidates to keep their Aadhaar biometrics permanently unlocked throughout the examination process. This is required for entry into the exam centre, identity checks, verification during the examination and exit from the centre. 
 Candidates who have selected the temporary unlocking option may have to change it to permanent unlocking to avoid problems during biometric verification. 
 The commission has also asked candidates to check and update their Aadhaar personal and biometric details, if required. They should also check whether their Aadhaar authentication is working properly before their examination date. 
 Candidates can lock their biometric details again after completing the examination if they want to. 
 The latest notice is based on UIDAI's rules for Aadhaar authentication and biometric checks. The aim is to make the identity verification process easier and avoid problems at examination centres. 
 Candidates should also remember that Aadhaar-based verification is optional under SSC's current Aadhaar policy. The new instructions apply to candidates who choose to use this verification facility.
